chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who began the day fasting in Ramadan, and when the day rose (midday), she became menstruating. He said, 'She breaks her fast.'
And I asked him about a woman who saw (signs of) purity at the beginning of the day. He said, 'She prays (Dhuhr and Asr) and completes her day (fast) and makes up (the fast) later.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who starts or ends her period during Ramadan fasting hours?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinct rulings for menstruating women in Ramadan, emphasizing that the onset of menses invalidates the fast immediately, while purity before noon allows for the continuation of the fast alongside the obligatory noon prayers (*Salat al-Zuhr*). The requirement to make up (*Qada*) the day even if purity occurs late in the day underscores the Shia view that the fast remains valid but incomplete without the concurrent performance of prayers, reflecting the jurisprudential principle that menstruation nullifies the fast but does not exempt one from the duty of retribution.
